water-stress induced down-regulation of the light-harvest complex and PSII proteins protects developing rice seedling from photo-damage.

drought stress induced down-regulation of the light harvesting complex and other proteins of the photosynthetic apparatus in the developing rice seedlings to protect the photosynthetic machinery from photo-damage and to reduce the generation of reactive oxygen species.

The main takeaway from our work is that

developing seedling under water deficit could reduce its light harvesting and photosynthetic apparatus in order to prevent the photo-oxidative damages, excessive ROS generation and membrane lipids peroxidation.
water-stress induced chloroplast development in rice seedlings is a protective mechanism against photo-oxidative injury.
